items.title: [Bug]: 较高版本 Transformers 与已知 Mindformers YAML 配置冲突，导致 AISBench 测试报错 TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MindformersTokenizer
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

Issue 标签: bug, MindIE, vLLM-Ascend, AISBench, compatibility, Tokenizer

环境信息:

硬件平台: Atlas 800I A2
推理框架：vllm-ascend 0.18.rc1
组件版本 (关键):
transformers: 较高版本 (>=4.40.0)
测试工具: AIS Bench
模型: Qwen3.5 (以及 GLM 系列，案例已于其他局点问题复用)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

问题描述:
在 Atlas 800I A2 单机上，使用 vLLM-Ascend 拉起 Qwen3.5 模型服务后，执行 AIS Bench 测试报错。错误日志如下：
`TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MindformersTokenizer with abstract method batch_encode_plus`
值得注意的是，其他测试方式（如 vllm bench）可以正常工作。

原因分析:

- 抽象类实例化冲突: 在较高版本的 transformers 库中，MindformersTokenizer 被定义为一个抽象类，强制要求其子类必须实现 batch_encode_plus 方法。这是 transformers 库为了规范化接口所做的更新。官方参考：[transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/bb0ee88a4a815302baab4cd41d1534b3fa318fab/src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py#L2544-L2567)
- 版本兼容性问题: 模型权重目录下（例如 ./model_path/）存在来自旧版 Mindformers 的 YAML 配置文件（如 predict_*.yaml）。这些旧版配置文件中定义的 Tokenizer 配置，在加载时尝试调用已被弃用或改为抽象方法的接口 batch_encode_plus，导致与新版 transformers 的抽象类定义冲突，初始化失败。

复现步骤:

1. 在 Atlas 800I A2 环境上，安装指定版本的 transformers (>=4.40.0) 和 vLLM-Ascend v0.18.0rc1。
2. 下载 Qwen3.5 模型权重，并确保权重目录下存在 Mindformers 风格的 YAML 配置文件（例如 predict_qwen3_5_8b.yaml）。
3. 使用 vLLM-Ascend 拉起模型推理服务。
4. 执行 AIS Bench 测试命令，观察错误日志。

issue复现情况：其他局点类似环境部署GLM测试时同样遇到此问题，并通过手动删除权重路径下的词表YAML文件临时规避。

临时解决方案/规避措施: 删除模型权重目录下的 Mindformers YAML 配置文件。
```
# 示例路径（Qwen3），具体路径取决于模型和部署方式
rm -f /model_path/predict*.yaml
```
原理: 删除后，vLLM-Ascend 将无法加载该冲突的配置文件，从而强制使用其默认或兼容的 Tokenizer 实现，绕过抽象类实例化错误，恢复 AIS Bench 测试流程。

根因定位:
根本原因是 旧版 Mindformers 的 YAML 配置文件与新版 transformers 库的 Tokenizer 接口定义不兼容。AIS Bench 测试的代码路径可能与其他测试路径（如 vllm bench）不同，触发了这个配置文件的加载，而其他测试路径则没有。

建议修复方向:

- MindIE/vLLM-Ascend 侧: 增强对模型目录下遗留配置文件的兼容性处理，例如，在加载 Tokenizer 时，优先使用 transformers 的标准 AutoTokenizer 逻辑，忽略或优雅降级处理不兼容的旧版配置文件。
- Mindformers 侧: 更新旧版 YAML 配置文件，使其 Tokenizer 定义与新版 transformers 库的抽象类接口保持一致。
- 文档/指南: 在昇腾模型部署文档中明确说明，对于使用 transformers 库的推理场景，需要清理模型目录下的旧版 Mindformers 配置文件。

items.title: [Question][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer: does the 640-token block table reach 32-pool pages on gfx942/gfx950 too?
items.bodyExcerpt:
We found this on hardware vLLM doesn't support (gfx1030, Radeon Pro V620), running GLM-5.3-Flash without aiter. The code path involved is shared with gfx942/gfx950, and we have no MI300/MI355 to check it on. Could someone with one confirm or rule it out?

**What we see.** `Glm5NextIndexerCache` stores pooled keys in pages of 32 pools (storage block 128 tokens at `index_kpool=4`). The hybrid KDA page rule makes the attention block 640. On ROCm the sparse-MLA and indexer backends accept `MultipleOf(16)` (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`), so `select_common_block_size` keeps kernel block 640. The indexer metadata builder only converts the table when the storage block is a multiple of the kernel block (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`, prefill and decode branches; unchanged on main):

```python
if (
    kernel_block_size is not None
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size != kernel_block_size
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size % kernel_block_size == 0
):
    factor = self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
    indexer_block_table = (block_table[:, ::factor] // factor).contiguous()
```

128 % 640 ≠ 0, so the 640-token table goes to `get_compressed_slot_mapping` (the kpool writer) and to `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` as if each entry named one 32-pool page. With per-chunk block allocation:
- pools written before their block exists land in padding;
- positions past the allocated blocks alias block 0;
- positions past the 52-column table (at `max_model_len` 32768) are masked by the gather.

On NVIDIA the kernel block is 64, so the `// factor` branch applies. As far as we can tell nothing here is aiter-specific: the kpool path uses `forward_cuda` on ROCm whether aiter is on or off.

**Reproducer.** One GPU, stock vLLM only, no model: [`repro_rocm_kpool_table.py`](https://github.com/Omnicef/vllm/blob/glm53-v030/tests/local/repro_rocm_kpool_table.py). It writes a 9,432-token prompt in the served prefill chunks with the real ROCm kpool writer

items.title: [Bug]: Any KV connector makes pipeline-parallel decode 50-90% slower on Model Runner V2 (all ranks reply, reply-ring writer spins holding the GIL)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.30.0 (official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` image), Model Runner V2 (the default for this architecture on 0.30) with async scheduling
- 2 nodes × 8× H100 80GB, pipeline parallel 8 × tensor parallel 2 (PP0–3 on node A, PP4–7 on node B)
- Model: GLM-5.2 FP8 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), `--max-num-seqs 8`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With pipeline parallelism across nodes on Model Runner V2 + async scheduling, configuring **any** KV connector makes decode much slower, even when the connector does nothing. We reproduced it with a trivial no-op connector (empty metadata, no loads or stores): it measures the same as our real connector.

Decode TPOT (steady state, `vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds` deltas, 12k-token prompts, 1024 forced output tokens, distinct prompts per stream):

| running requests | no connector | no-op KV connector | overhead |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 18.6 ms | 27.1 ms | +46% |
| 4 | 23.4 ms | 34.7 ms | +48% |
| 8 | 32.1 ms | 60.0 ms | +87% |

Throughput at 8 running requests drops from ~250 tok/s to ~133 tok/s. The same setup on the V1 model runner shows no overhead (18.3 vs 17.0 ms at 1 request).

items.title: [RFC]: Meta-device operator capture: see which operators a model runs on this platform, without weights or device memory
items.bodyExcerpt:
**Authors:** @sachinkademane, @imrkbhandari25

### Motivation.

Platform bring-up, kernel planning and performance modelling all start with the
same questions:

- Which operators does model X execute on platform Y, in what order, with which
  shapes and dtypes?
- Which attention, MoE and quantization backends did vLLM pick for it?
- Which kernels are missing on this platform, before downloading the weights or
  having enough devices to hold them?
- When a model or backend changes, which operators change?

Today the only way to answer them is to serve the model on real hardware under
the torch profiler. That means downloading the checkpoint and holding it in
accelerator memory. For current frontier models (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.3,
Kimi-K3, Ring-2.5-1T) that is a full node per question. Tracing with
`FakeTensorMode`/`make_fx` on a booted engine hides vLLM's custom-op bodies
behind their fake implementations, so the actual kernels are not visible either.

This RFC proposes **meta-device operator capture**. The model is built on
`torch.device("meta")` from its HF config alone, and one forward pass is
recorded. The **real `current_platform` makes every selection**: attention
backend, KV-cache layout and dtype, block sizes, MoE and quantization kernels,
IR op priority. Only the device is fake. There are no weights, no model-sized
device memory and no kernel execution.

Capture runs on a host of the target platform. Its vLLM build (the compiled
custom ops and their schemas) and a visible device drive platform detection and
backend selection, so XPU operators are captured on an XPU host and CUDA
operators on a CUDA host. One small device suffices for any model size: the
results below, up to DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Ring-2.5-1T, come from a single Arc Pro
B60.

- inputs for performance models and simulators (Chakra execution traces)

## Summary

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

## Safety

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.
- Non-indexer layers do not change the inputs to the remap.
- The default `index_topk_freq = 1` path is unchanged.
- Speculative decoding still remaps on every layer.

## Update: indexer and non-indexer layers are two KV cache groups

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53781  added the is_index_group_leader field to MLAAttentionSpec: `is_index_group_leader=self.indexer is not None,`. ), (

## Purpose

Two related changes, both following the review on this PR:

1. **Fix a soundness bug in `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_decode_logprobs_match_prefill_logprobs`.** The test rebuilt each prefill prefix from *text* and re-encoded it; `encode(decode(ids))` is not lossless for BPE tokenizers, so the "prefill" could evaluate a different token sequence than decode did and report false mismatches. The prefix is now built directly from token ids (`prompt_token_ids + decode_token_ids[:i]`), which also removes an O(N²) extra `llm.generate` per decoded token. This is the fix from #43317 (@Evangade), carried here at the maintainer's request after that PR went stale; the standalone tokenizer regression test from #43317 is dropped per the review there. Original report by @xRay2016 in #27433.
2. **Add `zai-org/glm-4-9b-chat` and `microsoft/phi-4` to the tested-model list**, following the [invitation to submit model validations without a separate issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53247#issuecomment-5374419058).

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`_nvfp4_compute_scale_factor` in `marlin_utils_fp4.py` finds the largest NVFP4 weight scale by materializing an FP32 copy of the whole scale tensor, a boolean mask, and a gathered copy of the positive entries. The MoE paths (`prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin`, `prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin`) call it on the scales of **all experts at once**, so for a 288-expert model such as GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 one call touches about 300M elements and allocates several GiB of transient device memory during weight loading. On unified-memory machines with little headroom at load time (DGX Spark GB10, #50925) that spike can fail the load or push the driver into the memory-pressure spiral reported by the community.

This PR reduces the input tensor directly. The returned factor is unchanged:

- a max commutes with the exact multiplication by `2**7`;
- non-positive scales never win the max when a positive scale exists, and an all-non-positive tensor still returns `1.0`;
- an empty tensor returns `1.0` as before.

One deliberate behavior change: a NaN scale now raises `ValueError` instead of being silently excluded from the max. Happy to drop that if maintainers prefer the old silent behavior.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A deterministic `persistent_topk` (the QSA / sparse-indexer block selection,
`csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh`) that is **also faster than the exact-topk workaround**
people currently reach for. The kernel returns a different result for identical inputs from call to
call: the **order** always varies, and when more keys share the threshold value than the candidate
buffers hold, the selected **set** varies too. Cause: output slots are handed out by `atomicAdd` in
thread-arrival order, and exact-key ties at the last radix round are taken first-come.

### Motivation update (2026-09-21) — read this before the original framing below

This PR was opened as a determinism fix. **On the evidence since, that framing overstates the
case, and I am restating it rather than leaving the body arguing something the threads have
undermined.** Three independent readings:

1. **Ours.** We censused the top-k boundary on real traffic: **0 ties at the k-th value across 6,192
   selecting rows** at 16k context ([09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55122#issuecomment-5602743511)).
   93 % of rows had fewer visible blocks than k, so selection was a no-op.
2. **The reporter of #51782.** @xueyangcs states the HPC-Ops TopK contract is **set-exact only** —
   with ties, any valid top-k set is permitted; set-stability was never guaranteed
   ([#51782, 09-09](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).
3. **An independent field report.** @NNNtrance replaced the selection with an exact `torch.topk` on
   GLM-5.3-Flash across three DGX Sparks and got **9/6 bad turns vs 11/7 stock — within noise**,
   while `index_topk 8192` gives 2/3. Selection accuracy was not their cause
   ([#51782, 09-12](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51782)).

So **the tie-ordering defect is real at the kernel level but does not appear to be reachable on the
traffic that motivated it.** What survives is the performance argument, which is independently

## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Auto-enable fp32 weights for the gfx950 router GEMM in GateLinear
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55351. The gfx950 low-M FP32 router GEMM added in #54845 never runs: `GateLinear` call sites (deepseek_v2, glm5next, deepseek_v4 nvidia/amd/cpu/xpu) pass the router dtype as `out_dtype` only, so the gate weight stays in the model dtype (bf16) and `allow_fp32_router_gemm` — which requires `self.weight.dtype == torch.float32` — is never true. The kernel is unreachable for the exact shapes it was instantiated for, e.g. DeepSeek-family `(6144, 256)`.

## Approach

Rather than updating every call site to pass `force_fp32_compute` (only nemotron_h does today), self-enable inside `GateLinear`: when `is_gfx950 and (input_size, output_size) in ROCM_FP32_ROUTER_GEMM_SUPPORTED_SHAPES and not bias`, set `force_fp32_compute = True` so the existing logic stores fp32 weights. One-site fix; the eligibility flags then light up through the normal path.

## What does NOT change

- CUDA paths (Hopper/Blackwell specialized kernels, bf16×bf16→fp32 epilogue): `is_gfx950` is false, guard inert.
- Unsupported shapes on gfx950 (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash's `(4096, 288)`): `is_rocm_fp32_shape` false, clean fallback.
- Biased gates: guard excludes bias (kernel/torch.mm path has no bias term).

## Verification

No GPU locally, so verified by simulation of the exact decision tree in `GateLinear.__init__`:

| Case | weights | fp32 kernel |
|---|---|---|
| gfx950, (6144, 256), no bias (issue repro) | fp32 | **enabled** (was: unreachable) |
| gfx950, (4096, 288) (GLM-5.3-Flash) | bf16 | unchanged fallback |
| CUDA H100, (6144, 256) | bf16 | unchanged |
| gfx950, biased gate | bf16 | unchanged |

`tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py` covers these flags with mocked platforms but requires a CUDA-built torch to instantiate `nn.Linear`; happy to run it on a gfx950 box if CI doesn't pick it up.

items.title: [Bugfix] Invalidate KDA merged conv-weight cache on weight reload
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55087. GLM-5.3 KDA merges the q/k/v short-conv weights into one cached tensor (`_merged_conv_weight`), built lazily on first forward. Online-RL workflows warm up with dummy weights (cache built), then refit `q_conv1d`/`k_conv1d`/`v_conv1d` — but the cached merge is never invalidated, so inference silently keeps using the pre-refit convolution weights.

## Approach

Weight loading dispatches on the param's stamped `weight_loader` (`getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` in `AutoWeightsLoader`). So the cache can be invalidated at exactly the point the weights change: in `Glm5NextLinearAttention.__init__`, wrap each conv weight's stamped loader so any write clears `_merged_conv_weight`. The next forward rebuilds it from the current params. No new hooks, no changes to the reload machinery.

## Coverage / limitations

- ✅ Initial load (loaders run before first forward; cache built after anyway)
- ✅ Checkpoint-format refit: `reload_weights` → `model.load_weights` → stamped loaders → cache cleared
- ✅ Layerwise reload: re-dispatches through the same stamped loaders
- ❌ Kernel-format refit (`param.copy_` bypass) writes params without loaders — the cache is NOT invalidated there. That path also skips every other derived-weight rebuild in the tree (same class of limitation); noted for follow-up if it matters in practice.

A `_version`-based approach was considered and rejected: the default loader writes via `param.data.copy_`, which bumps neither `param._version` nor `param.data._version` (verified on torch 2.10/ROCm), so version tracking cannot see the main refit path.

## Verification

|---|---|
| Build layer, populate merge cache | OK |
| Refit `q_conv1d` through its real stamped weight loader | cache **invalidated** |

items.title: [Bugfix] Skip FP8-dequant fast paths for PP-missing layers in GLM-5.3-Flash load
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #55725. GLM-5.3-Flash crashes at weight load on multi-node (2×8 H100) with `KeyError: 'layers.11.self_attn.fused_qkv_a_proj.weight'` on every second-node worker, while single-node runs fine.

## Root cause

With 2 nodes the run is pipeline-parallel (PP=2), so layer 11's params exist only on stage-0 ranks. The attached log (`layer11.log`) shows all `Worker_PP1_TP0..7` crashing; PP0 is clean. The normal load path guards every weight with `is_pp_missing_parameter` (glm5next/common/model.py), but the two FP8-dequant fast paths bypass it and index `params_dict` directly:

- `_try_load_fp8_attn_proj` → `params_dict[target_w]` (the traceback in the issue)
- `_try_load_fp8_indexer_wk` → `params_dict[fused_name]` (same class of hole)

On a PP rank that doesn't hold the layer, `params_dict` has no such key → KeyError before the normal path ever gets a chance to skip the weight.

## Fix

In both fast paths, return `False` when the target param is absent from `params_dict`, so the weight falls through to the normal path, which skips it via `is_pp_missing_parameter`. The indexer-wk guard is placed *before* buffering, so PP ranks also don't accumulate fp8 tensors that nobody loads. Behavior on ranks that hold the layer is byte-identical.

## Verification

No multi-node GPU here, so verified by driving both functions directly with the exact crashing weight names, on the MI350X pod against the patched module:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| PP1-style params_dict (layer 11 absent), fp8 `q_a_proj` weight + scale | not consumed, nothing loaded → falls to normal skip path (was: KeyError) |
| PP0-style control (BF16 `fused_qkv_a_proj` present) | consumed + loaded, unchanged |
| PP1, indexer `wk` weight + scale | not consumed → normal skip |
| PP0 control, indexer `wk` | consumed + loaded, unchanged |

Pre-commit: all hooks pass. Single-node (TP-only) behavior is untouched — the guards only trigger when the target param is missing.

items.title: [Perf][HiSparse] Avoid repeated prefix scans and residency updates
items.bodyExcerpt:
HiSparse's scheduler rescans the entire computed prefix on every materialization call, including pages already known to be durable. Each resident cache group also invokes the same shared materialization and residency operations. With 20 resident groups and hundreds of requests per rank, this consumed most of a scheduler CPU core and delayed workers before their DP collective.

This patch starts scanning at `max(ready_prefix_pages, importing_pages)` and invokes the shared operations only from the first resident manager. It preserves pending-write checks, holes beyond the durable prefix, spill budgets, import completion, and publication ordering. No serving configuration, routing, graph policy, or model math changes are included.

Two existing materialization tests now exercise both one and three resident groups, covering incomplete/out-of-order writes and per-step spill budgets.

### Performance evidence

B300, one EP8 prefill node and one EP8 decode node, 2,048-concurrent Scale-SWE agentic rollouts. GLM-5.3 NVFP4 (`RadixArk/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, revision `11af4cba759e6559eda70358a5778bd1bddddd78`), FP8 KV, HiSparse 300 GiB/decode GPU, index cache, NIXL and Mooncake, Rust frontend, natural routing. Decode used DeepEP LL and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE breakable graphs; EPLB, DBO and speculative decoding were disabled.

The same loaded deployment switched between the original implementation, cursor only, and the full fix. No reload, cache reset, eval restart, or serving-configuration change occurred between phases. The first 30 seconds of each phase are excluded.

On ROCm, MTP speculative decoding crashes for every GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 checkpoint on

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` runs once per KV-cache group per scheduler step and launches two GPU ops whose results are not needed:

1. **Unused `query_lens`.** `build()` computes `query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]`, but `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` only reads its size and device; the kernel derives per-request lengths from `cu_query_lens`. The parameter is dropped and `num_seqs` is taken as `cu_query_lens.size(0) - 1`.
2. **Self-aliasing `fill_`.** `paged_kv_indptr[n + 1:].fill_(paged_kv_indptr[n])` passes a view of the tensor being filled, so ATen clones the value first. A broadcast `copy_` from the same element writes the same values without the clone.

| op | aten ops | GPU kernels |
|---|---|---|
| `x[n+1:].fill_(x[n])` | `fill_` → `clone` (`empty_strided` + copy) → `copy_` | 2 |
| `t.copy_(x[n].expand_as(t))` | `copy_` | 1 |
| `qsl[1:] - qsl[:-1]` | `sub` (+ alloc) | 1 |

Each `build()` launches two fewer kernels and makes two fewer device allocations, with no change in output. #57885 removed a similar dead op from the DSA indexer builder.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Problem

A DEP32 GLM-5.3 prefill group (4 pods x 8 DP ranks, DeepEP) dies as a unit: one rank stops between steps, the other 31 wait for it in `internode_dispatch`, hit the 100 s DeepEP timeout and trap (Xid 43); the stalled rank never traps. Captured on a production group right after its first real requests:

- The stalled worker's main thread was in kernel state `D` inside `__vm_munmap` for 73 s, ran for 1 s, then in a 16 KiB anonymous `mmap` (`vm_mmap_pgoff`) for 88 s. `py-spy` could not attach for exactly that window, since it needs `mmap_lock` as well.
- `perf` on the same workers under load: 1,000-3,400 `mmap` + `munmap` calls per second per worker, all 16 KiB. CPython 3.12 allocates a new frame data-stack chunk with `mmap` when a call crosses the end of the current chunk and frees it on return (python/cpython#142183, fixed in 3.13.13); the MoE forward crosses that boundary in every layer.
- The node sat at its free-memory floor for the whole stall: MemFree 16 GiB against MemAvailable 896 GiB (about 700 GiB of clean checkpoint pages plus a 761 GiB CPU KV tier in shm), with direct-reclaim bursts (`pgscan_direct` 7k-20k per 5 s), `compact_stall` 23-56 per 5 s and hundreds of `thp_fault_fallback`. MemFree jumped from 17 to 344 GiB the moment the group died.

`mmap` and `munmap` take the process `mmap_lock` for write; a page fault takes it for read and, with no free pages, holds it through direct reclaim and compaction. items.title: [GLM5.3 Perf] Fuse Q projection with `fused_q` kernel, 1.27 ~1.64x kernel performance improvement
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fuse Q projection with `fused_q` kernel, removing one separate `torch.bmm` launch per attention layer.

All 78 layers are eligible: **78 fewer GPU kernel launches per TP rank**

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
import torch
import triton

from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.common.kernels import fused_q


@torch.inference_mode()
def benchmark(num_tokens: int) -> None:
    q = torch.randn(num_tokens, 16, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    q_nope, q_pe = q.split([192, 64], dim=-1)
    w_uk_t = torch.randn(512, 16, 192, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).permute(
        1, 2, 0
    )
    index_q = torch.randn(num_tokens, 32, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    index_weights = torch.randn(num_tokens, 32, device="cuda")
    positions = torch.arange(num_tokens, device="cuda")
    rope_cache = torch.randn(max(128, num_tokens), 64, device="cuda")
    q_scale = torch.tensor([0.37], device="cuda")

    def prepare(ql_nope, *, fuse_projection: bool):
        return fused_q(
            positions,
            q_pe,
            rope_cache,
            index_q,
            rope_cache,
            ql_nope,
            q_scale,
            index_weights,
            128**-0.5,
            32**-0.5,
            index_rope_interleave=True,
            quantize_mqa=False,
            q_nope=q_nope if fuse_projection else None,
            w_uk_t=w_uk_t if fuse_projection else None,
        )

    def baseline():
        ql_nope = torch.bmm(q_nope.transpose(0, 1), w_uk_t).transpose(0, 1)
        return ql_nope, *prepare(ql_nope, fuse_projection=False)

    def fused():
        ql_nope = torch.empty(num_tokens, 16, 512, device="cuda", dtype=q.dtype)
        return ql_nope, *prepare(ql_nope, fuse_projection=True)

    reference, result = baseline(), fused()
    torch.testing.assert_close(result[0], reference[0], rtol=0.02, atol=0.05)

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix GLM-5.3-Flash engine crash on slim images
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix an engine crash in the GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) vision tower when a request contains a slim image.

`Glm5NextVisionTransformer.rot_pos_emb` looks up every patch's cos/sin in the vision rope table, which `get_rope(..., max_position=8192)` fixes at 8192 rows. `Glm5NextProcessor` bounds images by pixel budget only and has no aspect-ratio cap. That is by design: `tests/transformers_utils/processors/test_glm5next.py` pins "extreme aspect stays proportional".

- A slim image therefore produces a grid whose long side exceeds 8192 patches. For example, a 200000×20 px image is accepted at 7143 tokens with `image_grid_thw = [1, 2, 14286]`.
- `get_cos_sin(14286)` silently returns only 8192 rows, and `cos[pos_ids]` reads past the end.
- On CPU that is an `IndexError`. On GPU it is a device-side assert that corrupts the CUDA context and takes down the EngineCore, so a single request can crash the server.

The Qwen2-VL and GLM-4V processors reject aspect ratios above 200, which keeps their grids inside the same 8192-row table. The GLM-5.3-Flash processor has no such cap.

The crash doesn't depend on checkpoint quantization or KV-cache dtype. The vision tower is built with `quant_config=None` and has no KV cache, and the `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` vision weights are BF16, the same as `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`.

**Fix:** `rot_pos_emb` now gets cos/sin through `_get_rotary_cos_sin`, which extends the table on demand. Existing rows are kept as-is, so results for every grid that fits the table are bit-identical to before.

**Not a duplicate:** On 2026-09-29 I searched open vllm-project/vllm PRs for `glm5next`, `rot_pos_emb` and `GLM-5.3-Flash image`, and issues for GLM-5.3-Flash image crashes. Nothing addresses this. The closest open PRs don't cover it:

## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot run with decode context parallelism. Its kpool sparse indexer compresses the indexer KV (`index_kpool=4`), and the indexer metadata builder rejects DCP whenever `compress_ratio > 1`. This check does not depend on the platform or the attention backend:

```
NotImplementedError: DCP is not supported with sparse indexer KV compression (compress_ratio=4)
```

This PR shards the kpool indexer across DCP ranks by pool:

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` must be a multiple of `index_kpool` (e.g. 4), so each compressed pool lives entirely on one rank. The builder now raises a clear error when this does not hold.
- `CompressedSlotMappingKernel` is DCP-aware. Each rank writes only the compressed states it owns, at rank-local positions. Prefill chunk metadata uses the interleave measured in compressed units.

## Purpose

`Glm5NextMoE` constructs `FusedMoE` with `n_shared_experts=None`, so `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is silently ignored for GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`). ## Purpose

This supersedes #55543 by @Leoyzen, who is kept as co-author. It enables the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM90 for rope-free sparse-MLA models with head_size 512, such as GLM-5.3-Flash, through `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Alternative to #57169 (and its earlier version #55219). It keeps #57169's GLM-5.3-Flash move to the generic packed KV layout with a `CircularBufferSpec` tail. It replaces the builder-side re-paging of the kpool indexer with a generic, worker-side kernel-block mapping per attention group. As a result, `BlockTable` / `BlockTables` stop knowing about kernel blocks.

**Design**
- **Block tables and slot mappings** are always in KV cache manager blocks, in V1 and MRv2. `kernel_block_sizes` is removed from `BlockTable`, `MultiGroupBlockTable`, `BlockTables`, both input batches and both slot-mapping kernels. Slot values are unchanged: `b*bs + off == (b*bpk + off//kbs)*kbs + off%kbs`.
- **Mapping per attention group.** When a group's backend needs blocks smaller than the manager's (`AttentionGroup.kernel_block_size`), `AttentionGroup.build_metadata` / `build_metadata_for_cudagraph_capture` / `build_metadata_for_drafting` map its block table to kernel blocks. Kernel block `j` of block `b` is `b * kernel_block_stride + j`. The mapped table goes into a persistent per-ubatch buffer (`kernel_block_table`), so CUDA graphs see a stable address.
- **Ordinary splits.** In a dense (unpacked) layout the stride is blocks-per-kernel-block. KV views are allocated in kernel blocks as before.
- **Packed compressed caches.** Example: GLM-5.3-Flash's kpool indexer, which DeepGEMM paged MQA reads in 32/64-state pages. `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache` re-strides the bound view over the packed blocks and takes the stride from the real tensor. It raises for token caches, which are written through manager-unit slot mappings.
- **Alignment.** A backend with only fixed kernel block sizes gets `block_stride_alignment = MultipleOf(max size)` (`customize_attention_spec`). `KVCacheSpec.get_block_stride_alignment()` resolves it in the engine against the *final* (possibly rescaled) block size, and returns 1 when the block runs whole.

Correct KV-cache handling for GLM-5.3's pooled sparse-MLA indexer (kpool) under prefill context parallelism (PCP). items.title: [Rust Frontend] Share tool schema views between argument coercion and grammars
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Rust tool parsers coerce raw parameter text by the tool's JSON schema (`tool/parameters.rs`), and argument grammars (#59395) constrain the same parameters by it, but each interpreted the schema on its own. Coercion ignored `$ref`: a parameter whose schema is `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"}` came back as the JSON text string `"{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"` instead of an object. Pydantic v2 `model_json_schema()`, which most SDKs use to build tool schemas, emits exactly this for nested models, enums, and `Optional[Model]`:

```json
{"$defs": {"Place": {...}, "Unit": {"enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "type": "string"}},
 "properties": {"place": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"},
                "unit": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Unit", "default": "celsius"},
                "backup": {"anyOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null}}}
```

This affects every schema-coercing parser: Qwen Coder and MiMo, GLM, MiniMax M2/M3, Hy. DeepSeek DSML and Kimi K3 decode by their `string=`/`type=` labels instead. Coercion and grammars also disagreed on `nullable`, `const`, single-schema `allOf`, and type-name aliases such as `"int"`, so a grammar could admit a value that the parser then decodes as another type.

Based on #59190, but not part of that stack. The open-PR search found #50933, which resolves `$ref`/`$defs` for the Python Qwen3-Coder path; there is no Rust counterpart. Python parity is not a goal here.

- New `schema::SchemaView` owns how a parameter's schema is read:
  - `resolve` follows local `$ref` chains and single-schema `allOf`; unresolvable, cyclic, and remote references accept any value and are never fetched;
  - `options` expands each reference target at most once per value, as the argument grammar walker in #59395 does, so shared definitions cannot blow up exponentially;
  - `options` splits a value schema into typed options: `const`/`enum` literals, one option per `anyOf`/`oneOf`/type-array alternative, `object`/`array` inferred from `properties`/`it

The shared FLA recurrent launchers in `vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/` put the batch x value-head product in `gridDim.z`:

Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

## Fix

Pass the kernels the last column, which is the per-sequence length. `[B]` and `(B, 1)` inputs, the C4A Triton path and the torch fallback are unchanged.

## Purpose

When KV cache zeroing is on (mixed KV dtypes, e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1, GLM-5.3-Flash), the worker zeroes newly allocated blocks. For an async KV load the scheduler exempts the blocks the load will write, since zeroing them would race the transfer. It derived that set from the token range `[local_hit, local_hit + external)`, which names the right blocks only for full attention. - A non-prefix-cacheable sliding window (DeepSeek-V4.1 bounded replay) gets no local-hit blocks, so the load allocates the whole kept window, including blocks below the local hit.
- A circular buffer recorded for zeroing (GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail) keeps its single block at index 0.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.

items.title: [KV Offload] Split the CPU offload region across shm files
items.bodyExcerpt:
Pre-faulting the CPU offload region is capped by its single `/dev/shm` file: page-cache inserts into one shmem file are serialized, so more workers or threads stop helping. On one H200 node, eight processes pre-faulting disjoint parts of a 64 GiB file reach 9.8 GiB/s in total. Given one file each, they reach 24.6 GiB/s, and sixteen files reach 44.8 GiB/s. #59430 hits the same ceiling with threads.

Split the region's rows over up to 32 files of at least 1 GiB each. The files are mapped back to back over one anonymous reservation, so the region stays contiguous. Workers with per-rank slots start pre-faulting on different files. Regions under 2 GiB, and other users of `SharedOffloadRegion`, keep a single file.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

Outside the replicated layout, ranks never read each other's slots, but they still share one region whose rows interleave all ranks. Every rank pre-faults and pins its strided slots in the same shm file, contending with the others.

Give each rank its own region holding only its slots, in its own shm file. No other process maps that file, so the rank no longer waits on the cross-worker barrier before unlinking it. The replicated layout keeps the shared region.
